data.title: TruGolf Announces Reverse Stock Split
data.description:
Salt Lake City, Utah, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TruGolf Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: TRUG), today announced a 1-for-5 reverse split of its Class A common stock. The reverse stock split was approved by the Company’s Board of Directors in accordance with Section 78.207 of the Nevada Revised Statutes and is intended to enable the Company to regain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market. Beginning on December 1, 2026, the Company’s Class A common stock will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Capital Market on a split adjusted basis under the trading symbol “TRUG” but will trade under the following new CUSIP number: 243733706.

As a result of the reverse stock split, every 5 shares of Class A common stock issued and outstanding as of the effective date will be automatically combined into one share of Class A common stock. No fractional shares will be issued if, as a result of the reverse stock split, a stockholder would otherwise become entitled to a fractional share because the number of shares of Class A common stock they hold before the reverse stock split is not evenly divisible by the split ratio. Instead, each stockholder will be entitled to receive a cash payment in lieu of a fractional share.

The reverse stock split will reduce the number of shares of outstanding Class A common stock from approximately 2.9 million shares, the number of shares outstanding as of the date hereof, to approximately 0.57 million shares. The par value of the Class A common stock will remain unchanged and the number of authorized shares of Class A common stock will be proportionately reduced to 2 million shares. The reverse split affects all stockholders uniformly and will not alter any common stockholder’s percentage interest in the Company’s equity, except to the extent that the reverse split results in some common stockholders owning a fractional share as described above.

About TruGolf

TruGolf Holdings (NASDAQ: TRUG) is where the consumer technology of TruGolf meets the institutional finance of Polymath. The Company is well positioned in tokenized finance while operating and growing a real technology business. Polymath develops enterprise-grade capital markets infrastructure for the issuance, compliance, and lifecycle management of regulated digital securities and other tokenized financial instruments. It enables issuers, investors, and market participants to create and manage tokenized representations of real-world assets within compliant frameworks, supporting investor onboarding, regulatory controls, and post-issuance administration across private and institutional markets. TruGolf is recognized as a leader in the golf simulator market, manufacturing and distributing cutting-edge software and hardware that redefines what is possible with golf technology. Its products are designed to capture the spirit of golf, blending tradition with modern innovation. Combined, these two businesses are well positioned in distinct growing markets but sharing the costs of one listed company. This is the power and potential of two digital native businesses working together.

data.title: KeyBank Offers Tips to Help Consumers Spot and Avoid Holiday Shopping Scams
data.description:
KeyBank Offers Tips to Help Consumers Spot and Avoid Holiday Shopping Scams

KeyBank Offers Tips to Help Consumers Spot and Avoid Holiday Shopping Scams

PR Newswire

CLEVELAND, Nov. 27, 2026

KeyBank shares warning signs and practical steps for avoiding phishing, fake shopping sites, payment app scams and other holiday fraud

CLEVELAND, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As holiday shopping picks up, so do opportunities for scammers.

Consumers shopping online, tracking packages, buying gift cards or donating to charities can encounter increasingly convincing fraud attempts. Scammers are also using artificial intelligence to create fake retail websites, emails, text messages and even AI-generated voices designed to impersonate trusted companies or people.

Knowing what to look for can help consumers recognize potential fraud before they share personal information or send money.

What are the most common holiday shopping scams?

Here are several scams consumers should watch for during the holiday season:

Bank imposter scams. Fraudsters may call, text or email pretending to represent a consumer's bank. They may claim there has been a suspicious transaction or login attempt, then ask for a one-time passcode, login credentials or debit card information. KeyBank will not initiate a call or text asking for your online banking username or password. KeyBank also will not ask a client to send money to themselves using Zelle®, an account transfer or a wire payment, or request remote access to your computer or mobile device. However, in some cases, we will call to verify your identity by asking for a one-time passcode that is sent to your mobile device.

Phishing and smishing scams. Fraudulent emails and text messages can look like legitimate communications from retailers, banks or delivery companies. Scammers may also use AI to create convincing fake retail websites and communications intended to capture debit card, credit card or other personal information. A common example is a fake package-delivery message asking for payment to release or redeliver an order.

Vishing and AI voice scams. Criminals can use AI-generated voices in phone calls to impersonate customer service representatives, delivery companies, family members or others in an effort to obtain sensitive information.

Payment app scams. Consumers should be cautious when an unfamiliar seller asks for payment through Zelle®, Venmo, Cash App, wire transfer or cryptocurrency. Recovering money sent to a fraudulent seller through these methods can be difficult.

Online marketplace scams. Fraudsters may advertise popular holiday gifts at unusually low prices, then request advance payment through a payment app, gift card or cryptocurrency before disappearing.

Gift card scams. Criminals may tamper with gift cards displayed on retail racks or convince victims to provide gift card numbers over the phone to make supposedly urgent payments.

Charity scams. The season of giving can also attract criminals impersonating legitimate charities or disaster-relief organizations through phone calls, texts, emails and social media.

5 ways to shop more safely this holiday season

A few habits can make it harder for scammers to succeed:

  1. Be skeptical of unexpected communications. Don't automatically trust an unsolicited call, email or text, even if it appears legitimate. Avoid clicking unfamiliar links or attachments and independently verify the communication using a known phone number, website or app.
  2. Monitor financial accounts regularly. Reviewing account activity frequently can help consumers identify unauthorized transactions sooner. KeyBank recommends clients check their accounts daily and report unauthorized activity immediately.
  3. Turn on multi-factor authentication. MFA provides another layer of account security by requiring an additional form of verification when signing in.
  4. Use secure internet connections. Avoid conducting financial transactions over public Wi-Fi. A secure Wi-Fi connection or virtual private network, or VPN, can help protect data.
  5. Look for buyer protection. When shopping through online marketplaces, consider platforms offering buyer protections and avoid paying sellers who cannot be independently verified.

Holiday scam warning signs consumers shouldn't ignore

Consumers should pause when they encounter:

  • A deal that seems too good to be true
  • An unexpected call, email or text
  • Pressure to send money or act immediately
  • Requests to keep a transaction secret
  • Requests for passwords, codes or sensitive financial information
  • Demands for payment through gift cards, cryptocurrency or payment apps
  • Last-minute requests to change payment information
  • Requests for remote access to a computer or device

These behaviors can indicate an attempted scam.

What should you do if you think you've been scammed?

Speed matters.

Consumers who believe they have been targeted or have already sent money should contact their financial institution immediately and report suspected fraud to the retailer and appropriate authorities. KeyBank clients can contact the KeyBank Fraud Client Service Center at 1-800-433-0124. Dial 711 for TTY/TRS.

Additional information about emerging scams, account security and fraud prevention is available at key.com/fraud.

Ultimately, one of the strongest defenses against holiday fraud is taking a moment before responding. An unexpected message, urgent request or unusually attractive deal is worth verifying independently before clicking a link, providing information or sending money.

ABOUT KEYCORP

KeyCorp's (NYSE: KEY) roots trace back more than 200 years to Albany, New York. Headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, Key is one of the nation's largest bank-based financial services companies, with assets of approximately $193 billion as of September 30, 2026. 

Key provides deposit, lending, cash management, and investment services to individuals and businesses in 15 states under the name KeyBank National Association through a network of approximately 950 branches and approximately 1,100 ATMs. Key also provides a broad range of sophisticated corporate and investment banking products, such as merger and acquisition advice, public and private debt and equity, syndications and derivatives to middle market companies in selected industries throughout the United States under the KeyBanc Capital Markets trade name. data.title: Sekur Private Data Deploys New User Interface for SekurMessenger, Incorporating SekurVoice
data.description:
MIAMI, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Sekur Private Data, Inc., a Miami-based Swiss-hosted cybersecurity, private communications, and defense communications company serving enterprise, government, and defense clients, and a wholly owned U.S. subsidiary of Sekur Private Data (OTCQB:SWISF)(CSE:SKUR)(FRA:GDT0) ("Sekur" or the "Company"), today announced that it has deployed a new user interface (UI) for SekurMessenger, its secure team messaging and collaboration platform, incorporating SekurVoice encrypted voice calling directly into the messaging experience. The new UI improves usability and the flow of functions across the application, making SekurMessenger much more user-friendly for the defense, government, enterprise, and executive users who rely on it every day. The Company has received great feedback on the new interface from users. The next phase of Sekur's product roadmap is completing the new SekurOne, planned for release by the third week of December 2026, before Christmas, with SekurVoice expected to launch as a separate plan and additional new solutions expected to be launched at the same time. These launches are part of Sekur's preparation for 2027, as the Company has started pre-sales efforts in the U.S. and internationally.

Bringing SekurVoice into SekurMessenger means users can move from a secure chat to a secure voice call within the same application, with a cleaner layout and a more logical flow between functions. The redesign is intended to make everyday tasks quicker and more intuitive, so that users spend less time navigating the application and more time communicating.

The new interface changes how SekurMessenger looks and works for the user, not how it protects them. End-to-end encryption, self-destructing messages, encrypted file transfers, Chat-by-Invite, and Sekur ID identity management with no phone number required all remain in place, built on Sekur's proprietary, Swiss-hosted architecture with zero reliance on Big Tech cloud infrastructure.

"Security only works if people actually use it, and that means the experience has to be as easy as the everyday apps people are used to," said Alain Ghiai, Founder and CEO of Sekur Private Data. "The new SekurMessenger interface, with SekurVoice built in, makes secure messaging and calling simpler and faster, and the feedback we have received from users has been great."

"This is the first step in a broader refresh of the Sekur platform. Our next phase is completing the new SekurOne, which we plan to release by the third week of December, before Christmas, and we expect to unveil more than just SekurOne at that time, including SekurVoice as its own plan. We are also already working on new interfaces for our admin panel, our registration process, and SekurMail, so that every part of the Sekur experience, from sign-up to daily use, meets the same standard."

Next Phase: SekurOne, SekurVoice, and Additional Solutions Planned Before Christmas

With the new SekurMessenger UI deployed, Sekur's development focus now turns to completing the new SekurOne, its fully encrypted voice/video, email, messaging, and VPN platform engineered on the proprietary HeliX data transfer architecture. The new SekurOne is planned for release by the third week of December 2026, before Christmas.

SekurOne will not be launched alone. SekurVoice is expected to launch as a separate plan before Christmas, giving clients the option to subscribe to Sekur's encrypted voice calling on its own, and Sekur expects to launch additional new solutions at the same time, with the unveiling planned before Christmas. Further details will be announced at launch. The timing and content of these releases are subject to the completion of development and testing, and there can be no assurance that they will be released on that schedule.

Preparing for 2027: Pre-Sales Underway in the U.S. and Internationally

The new interfaces and December launches are intended to prepare Sekur for 2027. The Company has started pre-sales efforts in the U.S. and internationally, including Africa, Latin America, the Middle East, and Central and Eastern Europe, and plans to enter 2027 with a refreshed, easier-to-use platform and an expanded set of solutions to offer enterprise, government, defense, and executive clients in those markets. Pre-sales efforts may not result in sales, and there can be no assurance as to the timing or amount of any resulting revenue.

New Interfaces Underway for Admin Panel, Registration, and SekurMail

Sekur is also developing a new UI for its admin panel, which organizations use to manage their users and accounts; a new UI for its registration process, to make it simpler for new users and organizations to sign up and get started; and a new UI for its SekurMail solutions, the Company's secure business and executive email platform.

Together with the new SekurMessenger UI and the upcoming SekurOne, these updates are intended to give Sekur's enterprise, government, defense, and executive clients a consistent, user-friendly experience across the entire platform, from onboarding and administration to daily secure communications.

Sekur Core Communications Solutions

Sekur delivers secure communications that work within and beyond the Sekur network, operating independently of conventional telecom infrastructure to reduce exposure to interception, SIGINT collection, traffic analysis, metadata exploitation, and hostile surveillance in contested environments. No Sekur solution data-mines or location-tracks its users.

All solutions are built on proprietary architecture with zero reliance on Big Tech cloud infrastructure, meeting the privacy, security, and OPSEC requirements of intelligence agencies, defense and federal organizations, military commands, diplomatic missions, government agencies, executives, and professionals handling CUI and other sensitive, mission-critical information. Deployments are supported by on-premises infrastructure options for full data sovereignty, mission assurance, and sole control over keys and data.

SekurOne - Encrypted Voice/Video, Email, Messaging, and VPN

A fully encrypted communications platform engineered on proprietary HeliX data transfer architecture, purpose-built to defeat telecom network tracing, resist Pegasus-style malware intrusion, and support CUI handling requirements. SekurOne is designed for defense and federal officials, military commanders, government leaders, and executives conducting confidential, operational, or sensitive conversations where standard carrier-based voice and video platforms present unacceptable interception and exploitation risk.

Call-by-Invite capability via SMS or SekurSend email ensures controlled access and eliminates unsolicited contact. Each user is assigned a unique Sekur ID for identity management, with no phone number required - preserving user privacy across all voice and video communications.

SekurMail - Secure Business and Executive Email

An enterprise- and government-grade encrypted email platform designed for defense and federal agencies, military commands, senior government officials, C-suite executives, and organizations handling confidential and operationally sensitive communications, including CUI correspondence. Built on proprietary architecture with zero dependence on Big Tech cloud infrastructure and no metadata tracking, SekurMail keeps sensitive communications private between sender and recipient.

Key capabilities include SekurSend/SekurReply for secure delivery to non-Sekur recipients without exposing sender identity or message content; full message delivery control and audit capability; encrypted file transfer; custom domain support for organizational integration; and active protection against phishing, social engineering, and Business Email Compromise (BEC) attacks targeting corporate and administrative networks.

SekurMessenger - Secure Team Messaging and Collaboration

A secure messaging platform providing end-to-end encrypted text, file transfer, voice messages, and collaboration capabilities for defense, military, government, and executive teams coordinating operational and mission-sensitive information, including CUI material. Features include self-destructing messages, encrypted file transfers, and compliance-grade archiving for recordkeeping and audit requirements.

Cross-network secure communications with non-Sekur users are supported via Chat-by-Invite, enabling secure coordination with coalition partners, external agencies, and field elements without compromising the network. Each user is assigned a unique Sekur ID for identity verification and contact authentication, with no phone number required.

SekurVPN - Enterprise Network Security and Identity Protection

An enterprise-grade Virtual Private Network leveraging proprietary HeliX encryption technology, engineered to provide secure internet access, identity obfuscation, and traffic protection for defense organizations, military and federal personnel, government agencies, and executives operating across remote, traveling, deployed, forward, or untrusted network environments.

SekurVPN maintains zero data logging, ensuring no record of user activity exists that could be exposed through legal process, network compromise, or third-party collection. It is built for defense, government, and executive use cases - including protection of traffic associated with CUI and operationally sensitive workflows - where standard commercial VPN solutions present unacceptable privacy and security risk.

SekurRelay - Executive-Level Secure Email Integration

An enterprise-grade secure email relay solution enabling domain splitting, which allows organizations to establish secure communications at the executive, board, or senior staff level without requiring full organizational migration or infrastructure overhaul.

SekurRelay removes one of the most significant barriers to large-scale defense, government, and enterprise deployment, enabling phased adoption that protects command leadership, flag officers, and the highest-value personnel and communications immediately while broader organizational rollout proceeds. It is designed for defense and government organizations, regulated industries, and enterprises requiring rapid, low-friction elevation of communications security at the command and executive tier, including environments handling CUI communications.

About Sekur Private Data
Sekur Private Data is a Swiss-hosted cybersecurity, defense communications, and privacy solutions provider, offering a secure suite of tools to protect governments, defense and federal agencies, businesses, and individuals from unauthorized access and cyber threats. With capabilities such as SekurOne, SekurMail, SekurMessenger, and SekurVPN, Sekur provides a reliable and secure means of digital communication and data storage for Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), classified-adjacent and civilian communications use, grounded in Swiss privacy standards with on-premises infrastructure for government agencies, allowing for data sovereignty. Sekur sells its solutions through its website www.sekur.com, approved distributors and telecommunications companies globally, and through the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Multiple Award Schedule (MAS), Contract No. 47QTCA18D0089 serving governments, defense institutions, federal agencies, businesses, and consumers worldwide. Sekur's main sales operations are in Miami, USA.

data.title: Clearing out my parents' house was a legal nightmare. How can I downsize without putting my kids through the same ordeal?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Some countercultural advice this Black Friday: stop buying stuff, plus other rules for downsizing

"Legal fees ended up eating up half the value of my parents' estate." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I have recently read and heard a lot about the recommendation for seniors to take an active role in managing their estates - specifically by downsizing, in addition to having the wills and estate plans you have advised for years. Downsizing means going through all the "stuff" accumulated over the years and weeding out the treasures and clutter we no longer use, need or want.

While many seniors do this when they move into a retirement community, plenty of us stay put in our homes for decades. My parents lived in their home from 1950 to 2020. They believed their children would enjoy going through their belongings and reminiscing after they passed, but the reality was quite different and a massive hassle.

None of us lived nearby, we argued over what to do with 70 years' worth of possessions, and eventually, lawyers and the courts got involved. Legal fees ate up half the value of my parents' estate. Downsizing is difficult because of sentimental attachments, the sheer physical energy it requires and the challenge of knowing what is valuable versus what to let go of.

In my own downsizing efforts, I've avoided the hassle of online listings, garage sales or hiring estate experts, opting instead to give things to neighbors, donate them to Goodwill or toss them. What advice can you share for seniors who have too much stuff, feel overwhelmed by the process and want to spare their families what mine went through?

Aging Downsizer

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: My husband wants to sell our $1.5 million home and downsize. But this is where we raised our kids - and I can't bear to leave.

You will be surprised how quickly you forget about items once they're gone.

Dear Downsizer,

Your experience clearing out your parents' home is a cautionary tale for children as well as parents.

Hiring lawyers can cost a fortune and escalate disagreements that could be better resolved with a mediator. When it comes to family, going to court should be the very last resort. Aging parents can start giving away their valuable items to their children in an effort to prevent arguments later on, or put in place a system for choosing them, such as labeling items or drawing straws and allowing each child to choose an item in rotation.

As I resist buying yet another pair of sneakers this Black Friday because, like you, I have too much stuff. I'm constantly wondering how much money I would have saved in my life had I stuck to a black cashmere turtleneck like Apple's (AAPL) late CEO Steve Jobs or a black leather jacket like Nvidia's (NVDA) newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang. Without further ado - and I hope this helps you - here are some tips for clearing your house.

5 rules of downsizing

(1) Be tough. Without throwing out something valuable like an antique, a letter from a loved one or a wedding photo album that can never be replaced, you have to be ruthless when downsizing. And while the struggle is real, you need to avoid engaging in it every time you open a box. Your memories are not packed away in an attic or basement. They are in your mind and they are in your heart.

(2) Think digital. If in doubt, take a snapshot so you won't forget what you are about to dump. You can take photos of a treasured childhood toy before donating it or throwing it in the garbage. And a Kindle (AMZN) or the Apple (AAPL) Books app takes up less space than thousands of physical books.You can always put your favorite memories on social media or put them in a shared online folder so family members have access to them.

(3) Take it easy. The emotional labor is as challenging as the physical labor. You are, after all, sifting through your memories, which will bring up good and possibly also bad or painful moments. Take your time. You acquired these belongings over a lifetime, so why would you put yourself through the onerous task of dismantling your life in a week or a month? Commit to one big garbage bag per day. If you do two per day, take Sunday off.

(4) Out of sight, out of mind. You will be surprised how quickly you forget about items once they're gone. Anyone who has moved house and lived without their belongings for a period of time will have experienced this. Our stuff becomes part of our identity. Sure, everyone has their own treasures - a piece of artwork that won't take up too much space on a wall - but you may be surprised how quickly you forget about items once they're out of sight.

The emotional labor is often as challenging as the physical labor.

(5) Stop buying. Some countercultural advice this Black Friday - stop buying stuff that replaces the stuff you threw out. Perhaps it's that 2026 holiday sweater that looks so enticing online, even when we have a closet full of old sweaters crying out to be worn. We all love a bargain, and Black Friday and Cyber Monday tempt us to spend, spend, spend (analysts forecast spending nearing $30 billion for both "consumer holidays" this year). Don't replace the stuff you throw out.

Make spring cleaning an annual or semiannual event. As writer Evelyn Richards noted in this personal reflection in Country Living Magazine about downsizing from a three-bedroom house to a one-bedroom apartment: "Decluttering isn't just about tidying up your home; it's also about nurturing your mental well-being. When you clear out the excess and organize your space, you create a serene and stress-free environment."

It feels lighter to walk into a room where everything is in order, she writes. "This kind of order can significantly reduce anxiety and make it easier to relax. When your home is clutter-free, it's like a breath of fresh air, allowing you to focus on what truly matters. Moreover, the process of decluttering itself can be therapeutic. As you sort through items, you make decisions about what to keep and what to let go, which can be incredibly empowering."

Clearing out old stuff is healthy. The ceramic bunny rabbit has got to go.

Related: This is the best Black Friday purchase I ever made

data.title: Stock Futures Jump as AI Trade Set for Rebound — Update
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

U.S. stock indexes are poised to open in the green for a shortened trading session Friday, as the artificial-intelligence trade rebounds at the end of a volatile week.

Nasdaq futures traded 2% higher, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.4% and 1.2%, respectively. If the gains hold to market close, the indexes will close a choppy week with gains of more than 4% each. Still, they remain well below their recent highs: The S&P 500 and Dow are each over 6% below their early October peaks, while the Nasdaq, down more than 14% over the same period, is still in a correction.

Signs of a rebound follow choppy trade earlier in the week. Stocks across the AI ecosystem rallied premarket, with Nvidia gaining over 3%, while chip makers and data-center providers looked set for strong opens. However, the AI trade isn't out of the woods yet, Amati Global Investors fund manager Mikhail Zverev said.

"We still haven't got answers to the biggest questions we are asking," the fund manager said. Concerns include "higher interest rates and the expanding cost of funding for the AI buildout," Zverev added.

Gains in the U.S. premarket followed a bullish session in Asia. South Korea's memory-chip-dominated Kospi jumped 4.3%, while stock indexes in Shanghai and Hong Kong rose after Chinese authorities reiterated their support for capital markets. European equity indexes rallied at the open, with AI-related stocks leading the charge. The continent's Stoxx 600 index rose 0.9% in afternoon trade.

Improved sentiment in equity markets bled into metals, too. Silver contracts jumped more than 9% to $43.68 a troy ounce, while gold futures added 3.6% to trade around $3,660 an ounce.

Oil prices continued to rise, with most-traded Brent crude contracts for February delivery nudging up 0.3% to trade close to $92 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contract added 1.7% to trade around $85.10 a barrel.

Treasurys weakened amid investors' shift back to risk and hardened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. Ten-year yields rose more than 5.5 basis points to trade above 4.900%, while two-year yields rose toward 4.700%. The Fed enters a blackout period on Saturday ahead of its December meeting, with expectations for a quarter-point rise priced in at 99%, according to LSEG.

The dollar edged higher against a basket of global currencies but remained below highs hit earlier this week. Bitcoin was helped by broader ebullient market sentiment, rising 1.5% to trade around $61,670.

Spanish voters head to the polls on Sunday as Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez looks to stay in power. Next week, Nvidia's reinstated Chief Executive Jensen Huang will appear in front of Congress on Tuesday and Wednesday.

data.title: New-home sales just hit a 2026 high as builders dangle low mortgages and Black Friday deals
data.description:
By Aarthi Swaminathan

Lower mortgage rates are one of the biggest factors spurring home purchases

The jump in new-home sales was surprising, and the "game-changer appears to be lower prices, especially for homes in the South," one economist says.

Sales of newly built homes surged to the highest level of the year in October, according to data released by the federal government on Wednesday, as builders offered aggressive discounts.

In October, new-home sales nationwide rose 14.2% from the previous month to the highest level since December 2025. The jump was in contrast to sales of existing homes, which fell 5.5% in October to a 16-year low.

The jump in new-home sales "was a surprise" and the "big game changer appears to be lower prices, especially for homes in the South," Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, said in a statement.

"What this [report] indicates is that price matters," she added. "The South has had more home building and more price reductions than other parts of the country, and buyers are responding."

The data come as would-be buyers across the U.S. struggle to afford homes. Homeownership has slipped out of reach for many Americans, particularly as the cost of gas and groceries have surged over the past year, on top of rising child-care, education and medical costs.

Elevated mortgage rates are also a barrier to entry for first-time home buyers, while stock-market volatility is spooking prospective buyers who have equity investments.

Sweetening the deal

The hurdles to homeownership continue to rise: To comfortably afford a typical home with a price of around $406,000, a home buyer would need to earn nearly $127,000. The median actual household income is about $87,000. The calculation on whether a housing payment is comfortable is determined by whether the annual cost of homeownership is no more than 30% of a buyer's annual income.

Against a backdrop of high costs across the board, builders are adjusting their prices to reflect what frustrated home buyers want.

New-home sales are faring better than existing-home sales as builders offer aggressive discounts to attract buyers. On top of price reductions, builders are also offering mortgage-rate buydowns, in which they pay to substantially lower buyers' mortgage rates for a fixed introductory period.

The median sale price of a new home sold in October 2026 was $391,300, down 3.2% from the same month a year ago.

Homeowners have been more resistant to price cuts when selling their home, as MarketWatch reported previously. The median price of an existing home sold in October was $416,700, up 0.4% from a year ago.

Even more builders were planning to drop home prices in November, NAHB survey data indicated, which could help drive sales through what is typically a slow season for the industry.

In Hockley, Texas, for instance, major national builder Lennar (LEN) cut the price of a four-bedroom, 2,013-square-foot home by $40,000 to $291,990 to lure buyers. Hockley is about 36 miles northwest of downtown Houston.

And Lennar is offering Black Friday sales on other new homes in greater Houston. Incentives include an adjustable-rate mortgage, or ARM, backed by the Federal Housing Administration, typically used by first-time buyers, with a rate as low as 3.99%, $40,000 price reductions and up to $7,500 off buyers' earnest-money deposit, which is the upfront money a buyer gives a seller after signing a contract to buy a house. The fine print indicates that this money comes back to the buyer as a credit, not as an upfront discount.

Lower mortgage rates are another major factor in boosting new-home sales, and builders are offering them in the form of temporary or permanent rate buydowns. A permanent buydown entails a lower rate for the life of the loan.

Even with sweeteners like these, most home buyers are still on the sidelines.

Max Slyusarchuk, founder and chief executive of AD Mortgage, told MarketWatch that, "as we enter the middle of the holiday season, we are coming to the slowest cycle in the housing market."

"While [mortgage] rates have started coming down, activity is still sliding the way it normally does this time of year, and in some cases it's slowed beyond the seasonal adjustment," Brent Busch, a Minnesota-based mortgage-loan officer, told MarketWatch.

"I attribute it to people being careful with their money right now," he added. "Between the stock-market swings and other market conditions, I feel people are taking somewhat of a 'wait and see' approach to finances, including mortgages."

-Aarthi Swaminathan

data.title: Bitcoin, Ether Rebound as Markets Stabilize — Update
data.description:
By Joseph Wilkins

Bitcoin rebounded above $61,000 on Friday as Asian markets stabilized and risk appetite returned to cryptocurrencies.

Bitcoin was 1.1% higher at $61,465, while ether gained 1% to $1,720. U.S. stock futures rose Friday following a break for Thanksgiving, with Asian markets taking cues. South Korea's Kospi rose more than 4%, with chip heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics jumping 6.4% and 4.5%, respectively.

Bitcoin's 90-day correlation to the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq-100 has rebuilt since reaching a year-to-date low in September, Block Scholes analyst Thahbib Rahman wrote in a note. Bitcoin's current correlation is 53% to the S&P 500 and 54% to the Nasdaq-100, up from 37% and 36% at the end of October.

Rahman said the flagship cryptocurrency could remain stuck as long as fears around the durability of the AI trade persist and drag down U.S. stocks.
